ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=x+b$ intersects the $x$ axis at point $C(4,0)$ and the $y$ axis at point $B$, and it intersects the hyperbola $y=\frac{m}{x}$ (where $x<0$) at point $A(-1,n)$. Connect $OA$. What is the sine value of $\angle OAB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $OM \perp AC$ at point $M$ through point $O$,\\
when $x=0$, $y=-4$, that is, $B(0, -4)$.\\
Since $OC=OB=4$,\\
Therefore, $\triangle OCB$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
Thus, $\angle OBC=\angle OCB=45^\circ$\\
Therefore, in $\triangle OMB$ $\sin 45^\circ=\frac{OM}{OB}$,\\
Thus, $OM=4\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=2\sqrt{2}$.\\
Therefore, in the right triangle $AOM$,\\
$AO=\sqrt{(-1-0)^{2}+(-5-0)^{2}}=\sqrt{26}$,\\
$\sin\angle OAB=\frac{OM}{OA}=\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{26}}}=\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{13}}{13}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, with the origin labeled O; a straight line with positive slope extends from the lower left to the upper right, intersects the x-axis at the right-side point C, and intersects the lower part of the y-axis at point B; in the lower left there is one branch of an inverse proportional function curve, the straight line and this curve intersect near the third quadrant at point A, and OA is connected in the figure. Reasoning: Point C(4,0) is on the straight line y=x+b, so 0=4+b, giving b=-4. Therefore the straight line is y=x-4, and it intersects the y-axis at B; when x=0, y=-4, so B=(0,-4). Point A(-1,n) is also on the straight line y=x-4, so n=-1-4=-5, namely A=(-1,-5). What is required is ∠OAB, that is, the angle with A as the vertex and formed by AO and AB. Starting from A, vector AO=(0-(-1),0-(-5))=(1,5), vector AB=(0-(-1),-4-(-5))=(1,1). The sine of the angle between the two vectors is |AO×AB|/(|AO||AB|)=|1·1-5·1|/(sqrt(26)·sqrt(2))=4/sqrt(52)=2/sqrt(13)=2sqrt(13)/13.
